name: linked-single-invocation-zero-bins
rationale: One invocation is bounded by source_size 1x1. The fixed channel loop advances its literal selector through the entry’s finite component count before exiting; it has no input-dependent trip count. Linking is enabled with one authored texture and one address-table element, while the exact callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing either resource. One-bin histogram parameters force each active channel to bin zero and make the poisoned counters observable byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-four-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2, 3, and 4 and receives exact float4 zero from all three linked _uber_clear bodies. A six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry swizzles it to float4(0,0,0,1), writes both required poisoned output textures, and captures binding zero byte-exactly.

name: two-gradient-function-constant-mix
rationale: Function constant zero is authored true so both conditional gradient resources remain live. The loop-free fragment samples two uniform one-pixel RGBA16Float textures, mixes their RGB values by an authored 0.5 scalar, leaves dimming disabled, adds its deterministic position-derived half noise, and writes the exact RGBA16Float result.

name: initialize-permuted-binning-counters
rationale: Five loop-free invocations exercise all four table-selected writes and the out-of-range branch. The first word of 256-byte records 4, 5, 2, and 3 becomes zero while exact comparison proves every other byte through the last accessed word remains poisoned.

name: fragment-varying-half4-with-viewport
rationale: The fragment returns its perspective center half4 varying unchanged while structurally accepting an unused viewport index; the generated fullscreen draw captures the color byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-six-2x2-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 6 and receives exact float4 zero from all five linked _uber_clear bodies. An eight-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x2 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x2 resource.

name: constant-buffer-float4-to-mrt4-highest
rationale: The loop-free fragment converts the exact finite float4 color in the 32-byte constant buffer to half4 and structurally inserts that same value into all four return members; selecting attachment three verifies the complete four-target aggregate mapping.

name: nan-model-functions-at-blend-and-rounding-edges
rationale: Metal's float functions at the NaN model's edges (DESIGN D293): lane i reads (a, b, t) and writes nan_functions' 36 words. Lanes: mix(a, b, t) at t = 0 and t = 1, at infinite and signed-zero endpoints and blend factors, and on lanes chosen so that the candidate compositions of the blend (fma(t, b, fma(-t, a, a)), its unfused variants, a * (1 - t) + b * t, and a + t * (b - a)) answer differently; then round and fract operands at signed zeros, small negatives, ties, and 2^23 neighbours. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: nan-model-functions-of-nan-operands
rationale: Which NaN Metal's float functions answer: lane i reads (a, b, t) and writes 36 words: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan of a; atan2(a, b); sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh, exp, exp2, exp10, log, log2, log10 of a; pow(a, b), powr(a, b); rsqrt, floor, ceil, round, trunc, rint, fract of a; dot(float2(a, b), float2(b, a)); length(float2(a, b)); mix(a, b, t); step(a, b); smoothstep(b, t, a); ldexp(a, 2); and the patterns of a and b. Lanes: each NaN as a (b = 1, t = 0.5) and as b (a = 0.5), two NaNs, a NaN blend factor, operands outside each function's domain and indeterminate forms (asin and acos of 2, log of -1, acosh of 0.5, pow of a negative base, functions of the infinities, inf * 0 in the dot product, inf - inf in mix), and controls. Compiled without fast math unless named; every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: half-division-under-fast-math
rationale: DESIGN D279 (WP-FMX2, refining D253.2 and D253.12): what Metal's half division x / y rounds to, compiled with the default fast math, so the fdiv half carries every fast-math flag: once to half, a float quotient rounded to half, or x times a reciprocal rounded first. Each of 512 threads writes x / y and 1 / y, each half zero-extended to a word, dividing by its own load of y (both copies hold the same value); words 2 and 3 keep the 0xAB poison. Operands (x, y): 192 generic quotients with exponents in [-6, 6]; 96 pairs where the once-rounded half quotient, x times a reciprocal rounded to half, and x times a float reciprocal rounded to half differ; 64 half denormal numerators, divisors, or quotients; 32 quotients near or past the largest half; 32 special pairs (zeros, infinities, NaN, the largest half, denormals, equal operands, quotients 1/3); the rest over the whole range. The AIR has no loop.

name: a-simdgroup-barrier-orders-threadgroup-words-between-lane-pairs
rationale: One threadgroup of 32 threads. Each stores 3t + 1 to words[t] of a static threadgroup array, waits at simdgroup_barrier(mem_threadgroup) (barrier.simdgroup, DESIGN D213), and reads words[t ^ 1], the word of the other thread of its aligned pair. Metal partitions a threadgroup into simdgroups of consecutive threads, so the pair is in one simdgroup at any even simdgroup width (Apple's is 32), and the barrier orders the store before the read: out[t] = 3 (t ^ 1) + 1. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirteen-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 13 and receives exact float4 zero from all twelve linked _uber_clear bodies. A fifteen-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: a-simdgroup-and-a-half-return-before-the-first-barrier-and-more-before-the-second
rationale: One threadgroup of 96 threads (three simdgroups), limits (50, 20): threads 50..95 (the tail of simdgroup 1 and all of simdgroup 2) return before the first barrier, threads 20..49 (the tail of simdgroup 0 and the rest of simdgroup 1) between the barriers, and threads 0..19 pass both. Q3 model (control Q3, DESIGN D2.3): invocations that returned are absent from later barriers, which the fuel's forced return relies on. Threads t >= limits[0] write 0xE0000000 | t and return before the first threadgroup barrier; the rest store a[t] = 3t + 1 to threadgroup memory, pass the barrier and read a[(t + 1) mod limits[0]]; of those, threads t >= limits[1] write 0xE1000000 | that word and return between the barriers; the rest store b[t] = word + 1000, pass the second barrier and write b[(t + 5) mod limits[1]]. Every word read was stored before the barrier the reader passed, and only by threads that reach it, so the remaining threads' words are exact only if each barrier synchronised exactly them. AGX runs the pattern (control section 4.4: formally undefined in Metal, relied on in practice); this case records it. Every thread writes its own word once, on the path it takes, and every word differs from the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop; the threadgroup arrays are static (128 words each).

name: three-threads-return-before-the-first-barrier-and-all-but-seven-before-the-second
rationale: One threadgroup of 64 threads (two simdgroups), limits (61, 7): threads 61..63 (three lanes of simdgroup 1) return before the first barrier, threads 7..60 between the barriers (all of simdgroup 1 that is left and simdgroup 0 but its first seven lanes), and threads 0..6 pass both. Q3 model (control Q3, DESIGN D2.3): invocations that returned are absent from later barriers, which the fuel's forced return relies on. Threads t >= limits[0] write 0xE0000000 | t and return before the first threadgroup barrier; the rest store a[t] = 3t + 1 to threadgroup memory, pass the barrier and read a[(t + 1) mod limits[0]]; of those, threads t >= limits[1] write 0xE1000000 | that word and return between the barriers; the rest store b[t] = word + 1000, pass the second barrier and write b[(t + 5) mod limits[1]]. Every word read was stored before the barrier the reader passed, and only by threads that reach it, so the remaining threads' words are exact only if each barrier synchronised exactly them. AGX runs the pattern (control section 4.4: formally undefined in Metal, relied on in practice); this case records it. Every thread writes its own word once, on the path it takes, and every word differs from the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop; the threadgroup arrays are static (128 words each).

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-four-threadgroup-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2, 3, and 4 and receives exact float4 zero from all three linked _uber_clear bodies. A six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The single-invocation threadgroup executes both barriers over internal static storage and writes the linked result to the poisoned primary texel byte-exactly.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-nine
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 29 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-eight linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-one-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; the final selector reads register 2 and writes exact zero to the poisoned primary texel.

name: sign-of-negative-zero-through-the-l1-regularizer
rationale: The parameter block selects regularization type 1, the only arm that calls air.sign.f32, and zeroes the gradient scale so the update reduces to out = w - learningRate * (sign(w) * regularizationScale). With learningRate -1 and regularizationScale 1 that is exactly w + sign(w), so each of the four threads writes an authored function of its own weight. Lane 0 uses -0.0 to read the sign of zero back out: Metal Shading Language documents sign(-0.0) as -0.0 while GLSL.std.450 FSign -- what this translator emits for air.sign -- answers +0.0, and since (-0.0) + (-0.0) is -0.0 while (-0.0) + (+0.0) is +0.0, the written sign bit reports which one ran. Metal writes 0x00000000: this module carries no-signed-zeros-fp-math, the hardware does not preserve the sign of the zero, and FSign is the lowering that matches what Metal actually computes. Lane 1 is the +0.0 control, and lanes 2 and 3 (-3 and 5) answer -4 and 6 under either reading, proving the dispatch ran.

name: float-to-bool-at-every-special-value-without-fast-math
rationale: The twin of float-to-bool-at-every-special-value (same inputs, same output layout; read that rationale): the same program compiled -fno-fast-math, so the module records air.compile.fast_math_disable. For L1d. If the two observations differ on a NaN, infinity, or denormal lane, what air.convert to i1 computes depends on the module's fast-math option, and a lowering has to read it from the compile options. If they agree, the options do not matter.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-seventeen-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 17 and receives exact float4 zero from all sixteen linked _uber_clear bodies. name: an-integer-threadgroup-address-reaches-metals-layout
rationale: An integer threadgroup address (an inttoptr of a literal, the shape of corpus row 434cde47's atomic subtract at byte 1024) names a byte of Metal's threadgroup layout, which AIR does not carry. Probes on an M3 Max and an M4 measured the layout: a kernel's static threadgroup objects lie in the reverse of the order of their last references in the function, each aligned to its alignment and to at least 4, from 0. Here the module declares colors, bases, centers and references each once, in the other order (as in the corpus row), so the reverse of the module order would place them differently: colors (half4[256]) lies at 0, bases (float4[256]) at 2048, centers (float2[256]) at 6144. Thread 0's atomic subtract of 1 at byte 1024 turns colors[128]'s first word (two halves of 128.0, 0x58005800) into 0x580057ff, and its store of 0xC0FFEE at byte 2064 replaces bases[1].x; every other word is the thread's own value. Each thread writes its elements of all three arrays after the second barrier, so a translation that lays the arrays out in another order, or refuses the literal, fails exactly those two words.

name: pow-reapplies-the-sign-the-exponent-parity-earns
rationale: GLSL.std.450 `Pow` is not Metal's `pow` twice over, and `lower_metal_pow` -- which 984 of the 14579 corpus sources reach -- has to close both gaps with arithmetic no corpus shader can reach the corners of. SPIRV-Cross renders `Pow` as MSL `powr`, so on the device the magnitude is `powr(|x|, y)`: device-measured, that differs from `pow` for a non-negative base on exactly two rules -- `powr(0, 0)`, `powr(inf, 0)` and `powr(NaN, 0)` are NaN where `pow` is 1, and `powr(1, +-inf)` is NaN where `pow` is 1. And `Pow` has no negative base at all, so the sign is reapplied by the exponent's parity, which negative zero (whose sign an odd integer exponent still carries, and which fails `x < 0`) and negative infinity (which a non-integer exponent does NOT take out of the domain, unlike a finite negative base) both get wrong under the obvious rule. This is the whole 7 x 12 input space of those guards: bases +0, -0, -2, -1, -inf, +inf, +2 against exponents 3, -3, 2, -2, 0.5, 2.6, 0, -0, +inf, -inf, qNaN, 1, so every combination of (sign of base, finiteness of base, integrality of exponent, parity of exponent, sign of exponent) appears and each guard has a lane that fails without it. The base +2 substitutes exponent 4 for 0.5 and -1 for 2.6, the only two lanes whose answer would be irrational; every other answer is exactly 0, +-1, +-2, 4, +-8, 0.125, 0.25, 16, +-inf or NaN, so the comparison is exact bytes. Three channels per lane ask `air.pow.f32`, `air.fast_pow.f32` and `air.pow.f16`, which is every width and variant that reaches this one lowering.

name: blit-a-staging-rectangle-with-the-swizzle-function-constant-set
rationale: The same blit with swizzleBGRA supplied as true, which selects the BGRA arm of the select the constant's VALUE drives. Paired with the unset case it pins that the function constant reaches the lowering as a value rather than only as a defined-ness predicate: the two differ in exactly one byte of input and must differ in the red and blue channels of every one of the four output texels.

name: blit-a-staging-rectangle-with-the-swizzle-function-constant-unset
rationale: The kernel widens a uchar3 through air.convert.f.v3f32.u.v3i8, scales by 1/255 and writes it to an rgba8_unorm target, so every byte round-trips exactly and an exact comparison is legitimate. The channel order is chosen by the VALUE of the swizzleBGRA function constant rather than by a defined-ness predicate; with no value supplied it folds to zero and the straight RGBA arm is selected. The blit rectangle carries width 2, which is also the staging row stride, so reading the rectangle wrong reads the wrong staging texel; all four texels differ in every channel so a swizzle or a stride error is visible.

name: map-screen-coordinates-through-a-pointer-array-of-rate-maps
rationale: Metal ground truth for rasterization-rate maps picked from a thread-memory array of their pointers (DESIGN D240), the placement a corpus row reads its map from: the kernel stores the addresses of buffers 0 (`left`) and 1 (`right`) in a local two-element array, kept as an alloca, and maps through the pointer it loads at index tid.y, so grid row y = 0 maps through `left` and row y = 1 through `right`. Both buffers are authored as `rasterization_rate_map`: the Metal oracle binds what copyParameterDataToBuffer:offset: writes for the map newRasterizationRateMapWithDescriptor: compiles, and a Vulkan executor this crate's parameter data of the same map (bind::RasterizationRateMap). `left` is a 64x64 map of uniform quality 1.0 (the identity) and `right` is 37x23 with horizontal samples [0.5, 1] and vertical samples [1, 0.5], the two maps whose tiles this crate compiles as Apple M3 does (DESIGN D235.8). The screen coordinates (0, 0), (1.5, 2.5), (10.25, 7.75), (17.5, 11.5), (20.125, 3.875), (31.25, 20.75), (35.5, 21.5), (5, 18) lie inside both screens at exact binary fractions; through `right` seven of them move along x (this crate's decoder answers 1.4545455, 9.939394, 16.969698, 19.515152, 30.303032, 34.5, 4.848485) and y is the identity. Output: sixteen float2 (row-major lanes, x then y bits) into buffer 2.

name: float4-to-half4-varying-conversion
rationale: The generated companion supplies a finite float4 perspective varying; the fragment converts every lane to half and writes the result byte-exactly.

name: scatter-sixteen-residues-into-a-bucket-major-offset-table
rationale:
A radix-16 reorder pass built from two stable radix-4 counting sorts, whose per-bucket counter is the ushort4 that air.simd_prefix_exclusive_sum.u.v4i16 scans: each thread turns its 2-bit sub-digit into a one-hot ushort4, so lane k of the vector counts the items whose sub-digit is k. Both prefix-sum sites run twice (the sort loop is exactly two passes at bit positions 4*digit and 4*digit+2), and the keys are chosen so all four lanes carry 16 rather than leaving three of them zero.
The threadgroup is 64 threads = two simdgroups, which is the smallest size that makes the cross-simdgroup scan carry a real value instead of a degenerate zero; it is also a multiple of the simdgroup width, which the kernel requires -- only lane simd_width-1 writes its simdgroup's slot of the shared vector, so a partial trailing simdgroup would leave that slot undefined. Two threadgroups make num_groups=2 meaningful, since num_groups is the STRIDE of the offsets table: the kernel reads offsets[bucket*num_groups + group], bucket-major, unguarded.
num_keys is exactly group_size*num_groups, so no thread carries the INT_MAX/0xFFFFFFFF sentinel that an out-of-range thread would otherwise sort into bucket 15 and scatter over the next group's region. offsets is set to the true exclusive prefix scan of the (bucket, group) histogram, so the destinations are exactly {0..127} and no output word keeps its poison.
keys are i%16 and indices are i, so bucket b of group g holds threads b, b+16, b+32, b+48 in that order and the answer is forced by stability alone: reordered_indices[p] = p/8 + 16*(p%8). The expectation is derived from that closed form rather than by simulating the two sort passes, so the case checks the kernel rather than restating it. Digit 0 also pins that the bucket is taken from the unsigned key with no sign flip -- the module contains no xor with 0x80000000 at all.

name: define-a-clipping-constant-false-and-gain-a-stage-in-location
rationale:
sixChannelBlend_copyToCanvas asks whether its `CLIPPING` function constant was DEFINED, and the answer gates a stage-in location: `pixelCoord` carries `air.function_constant` naming the implicit predicate `CLIPPING_DEFINED`, so a caller who supplies the constant hands the fragment three varyings and a caller who does not hands it two. The value itself is never read by the entry. These three cases run the same three texels through all three definedness arms -- not supplied, supplied false, supplied true -- and must produce the same colour, so the assertion is that the stage-in signature moves underneath a result that does not.

A fragment case cannot choose its varyings, so every input texture is one texel: under the constexpr `clamp_to_edge` sampler a one-by-one texture returns that texel at any coordinate and the linear filter blends it with itself, which takes the unknown interpolated coordinates out of the derivation entirely. The colour is `multiply * content + add` with the alpha lane then overwritten by 1: 4*0.5 + 0.125, 8*0.25 + 0.0625, 0.5*2 + 1, and 2*0.75 + 0.5 = 2 discarded for the constant. Every product and sum is a dyadic rational inside binary16, so a contraction into an FMA cannot change the answer. The alpha lane is the one that names the `insertelement`: without it the target would read 2.0 rather than 1.0. The two multiplicands commute, so this case pins the addend, the alpha override and the definedness -- not which of `contentImage` and `multiplyImage` is which.

This case supplies false, so `pixelCoord` joins the stage-in layout on the strength of definedness alone -- the constant reads as off and the location appears anyway.

name: define-a-clipping-constant-true-for-the-same-blended-texel
rationale:
sixChannelBlend_copyToCanvas asks whether its `CLIPPING` function constant was DEFINED, and the answer gates a stage-in location: `pixelCoord` carries `air.function_constant` naming the implicit predicate `CLIPPING_DEFINED`, so a caller who supplies the constant hands the fragment three varyings and a caller who does not hands it two. These three cases run the same three texels through all three definedness arms -- not supplied, supplied false, supplied true -- and must produce the same colour, so the assertion is that the stage-in signature moves underneath a result that does not.

This case supplies true, which differs from the false case only in the byte the specializer writes into the initializer. Both are defined, so both carry three varyings and both must land on the same texel.

name: linked-single-unit-ArrayMultiplyTTLinking
rationale: One invocation multiplies a 1x1 matrix pair with K equal to one. Matrix dimensions, batch counts, split counts, and NDArray extents are one; row and allocation byte strides are the exact four-byte float width, bounding every matrix and batch loop. The array declares three elements. Metal reports the third as `missing Buffer binding at index 2 for buffers.2[0]`, so every earlier observation of this case read undefined memory for it. It is authored 3.0, distinct from the 1.0 of element zero, and the written value was measured invariant under it: setting the operand pair to 2.0 and 3.0 also writes zero. This case pins the zero the linked kernel writes, not a product.

name: measure-a-signed-distance-gradient-across-one-pixel
rationale:
sprite_sdf_alpha_fragment antialiases a signed-distance sprite by dividing the distance by the screen-space width of one distance unit, and that width is the only place `air.dfdx.f16` and `air.dfdy.f16` appear: it takes both derivatives of the sampled distance, widens them to float, and passes their length through `air.fast_sqrt.f32` and a 0.75 scale. The quotient `(sdf - 0.5 + m) / 2m` is then clamped to [0,1] and smoothstepped, so the whole fragment is a function of the sampled distance and that one derivative magnitude.

A fragment case cannot choose its varyings, but it can choose the texture the varying indexes. The harness's generated vertex shader hands `float2 texCoord` the value `uv = (p+1)/2` over a fullscreen triangle, so at pixel (px,py) of a W-by-H target `uv.x` is exactly `(px+0.5)/W`. A W-wide texture under a nearest, normalized, clamp-to-edge sampler -- which this case supplies, since both samplers are runtime arguments rather than constexpr -- therefore returns texel px at pixel px. `uv.y` is the flipped `1 - (py+0.5)/H`, and this case sidesteps that entirely: every texture row is identical, so the answer does not depend on which way the vertical axis runs.

That also makes the derivative exactly authored. The distance varies only along x, so `air.dfdy.f16` must be zero and `air.dfdx.f16` is the difference across each two-pixel quad column, which every column pair here sets to 3. The magnitude is then `0.75 * sqrt(9 + 0) = 2.25`, and because that float is truncated to half before it is used, a fast square root's last-bit error cannot reach the answer: the nearest half to 2.25 is 2.25 and its neighbours are 1/512 away.

Every one of the twelve distance values is chosen so the clamped quotient is exactly 0, exactly 0.5 or exactly 1 -- never a fraction whose exactness would depend on whether the fast-math `fdiv` divides or multiplies by a reciprocal. Two of them sit exactly on the clamp boundaries: at sdf = -1.75 the numerator is exactly zero and at sdf = 2.75 it is exactly the denominator, which is where the case gets its grip on the derivative. Both are inside the band a doubled derivative would open -- a translator that measured the gradient across the whole quad rather than across one pixel would send the first to 0.25 and the second to 0.75, and the smoothstep turns those into 0.15625*alpha and 0.84375*alpha instead of 0 and alpha. The alpha texture carries a distinct sixteenth per column, so each of the twelve columns states its own arm.

name: measure-the-same-gradient-along-the-other-axis
rationale:
The companion case to `measure-a-signed-distance-gradient-across-one-pixel`, turned ninety degrees. There the sampled distance varied only along x, so `air.dfdy.f16` had to be zero and `air.dfdx.f16` carried the whole magnitude; here it varies only along y, so the two swap roles. The shader only ever uses the length of the two derivatives, so neither case can see a pure swap of the two -- both produce the same magnitude, 3, and the same 0.75 * sqrt(9) = 2.25 scale. What the pair does pin is each derivative separately: this case fails if `air.dfdy.f16` is dead, and its companion fails if `air.dfdx.f16` is, because in each the other derivative is genuinely zero and the whole magnitude rests on one call.

The harness's fullscreen vertex shader hands `texCoord` the value `uv = (p+1)/2`, whose vertical half runs opposite to the framebuffer: `uv.y` at pixel py of an H-tall target is `1 - (py+0.5)/H`, so a nearest normalized sampler over an H-tall texture reads row H-1-py. This case does not have to know which way that runs. Both textures are palindromic in y -- row r and row H-1-r are equal -- so every pixel samples the same distance and the same alpha under either convention, and each quad's two rows sample the same pair either way, which leaves the derivative unchanged in sign as well as in magnitude.

The sixteen rows step through the same arms the x case does: the clamped quotient is exactly 0, exactly 0.5 or exactly 1 at every row, never a fraction whose exactness would turn on how the fast-math `fdiv` is implemented. Row 3's distance of -1.75 makes the numerator exactly zero and row 6's 2.75 makes it exactly the denominator; a derivative measured across the whole quad instead of one pixel would open the band and move both off their clamps. The alpha texture varies along x as well as y, so the two columns state the same distance arm at two different alphas.

name: single-instance-acceleration-structure-intersection

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eighteen-threadgroup-primary

name: linked-k48-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-64-transposed
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-K case of this entry (DESIGN D296; WP-EVG, TODO 6.2), whose K = 0 stops the kernel before its arithmetic. One threadgroup of 128 lanes (4 simdgroups) runs the single 64x64 output tile: B = 1, M = N = 64, K = 48, so the tile is full in M and N (the unsafe loader path) and K runs one whole 32-deep block and a 16-deep remainder (the safe loader). The user constant keeps 8-bit unsigned weights, group size one, no bias, the non-cooperative loader; constant 122 binds a two-entry table (1 source, 1 destination). x is [M][K] (x_ld = 48) and every row holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 repeating, so every row of the result is the same: the linked destination callback, which writes table entry 1 at the column coordinate only, stores one value per column from every row, the same value, so the 64 words observed (offset 0, 256 bytes) do not depend on write order. W[n][k] (row stride w_ld = 48 bytes) holds q(n, k) = (11n + 3k + floor(3nk/5)) mod 16, nonlinear in n, so the column sums differ (63 of the 64 distinct whichever scale element the layout reads) and a column computed from another column's weights changes its word; scales and biases (scales_ld = biases_ld = 1, sized N*K) repeat 0.5, 1, 2 and 0, 1, 2, 3 (biases unread without the bias bit). Each dequantized weight is q * s, a multiple of 0.5 at most 30, exact in float and in the threadgroup tile; each product with x is a multiple of 0.5 at most 150 and each sum of 48 at most 7200, below 2^13: exact in float in any order or contraction, and on the float inputs.

name: linked-zero-k-quantized-matrix-multiply-float-64-transposed
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: A float counterpart of the committed qmm_t_64_bfloat case (DESIGN D272): qmm_t_64_float with the same function constants, resources, one-thread dispatch, and linked visible functions (postfixPrimary_4xf, postfixPrimary_f). Its zero extents keep every loop bound finite, so the case observes the four-byte destination allocation; the kernel links translation units each with its own static initializer and no llvm.global_ctors list, and calls matmul2d, so its translation exercises the unordered-initializer rule (D272.4) and the matmul2d lowering (D272.3). Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: visible-table-clear-slot-two-rgb-lane-output
rationale: One invocation takes the non-empty path because the authored bounds are float2(1), calls visible-function-table slot 2, and receives exact float4 zero from the linked _uber_clear body without dereferencing callback arguments. Eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds, with register 2 selected as the result. This entry splats the linked result R, G, and B lanes into three adjacent poisoned RGBA32 pixels; the complete 3x1 footprint is selected for byte-exact comparison.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirty-dual-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 30 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-nine linked _uber_clear bodies. A thirty-two-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. This entry writes the selected zero to both required poisoned output textures, with binding zero captured byte-exactly.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.
